paras: Bofa erlangeri, also known commonly as the Ethiopian house snake, is a species of snake in the family Lamprophiidae. The species is endemic to Ethiopia.
Bofa erlangeri is the only species in the genus Bofa.
The specific name, erlangeri, is in honor of German ornithologist Carlo von Erlanger, who was one of the collectors of the holotype.
Bofa erlangeri is found in the central plateau of Ethiopia.
The preferred natural habitat of B. erlangeri is forest, at altitudes of 800–2,800 m (2,600–9,200 ft), and it has also been found in farmland.
Bofa erlangeri may attain a total length (including tail) of 1.2 m (3.9 ft).
